Methodology.metadataDescription: How WC26 Transfer Intelligence interprets player evidence and ranks replacement candidates.
Methodology.title: Similarity is evidence, not the final decision
Methodology.description: WC26 Transfer Intelligence combines statistical, tactical, spatial, heatmap, quality, reliability, age and market evidence to rank replacements for a specific recruitment objective.

core.title: The objective is not to find the most similar player. It is to find the most suitable replacement for the selected recruitment context.
core.description: Statistical similarity describes profile resemblance. The final recommendation also considers tactical fit, occupied areas, tournament quality, evidence reliability, age and market value.

pipeline.title: From target player to ranked candidates

selectTarget.title: Select the target
selectTarget.description: The analysis starts from one stable player identity and its tournament, role, spatial and market profile.

buildCandidatePool.title: Build the candidate pool
buildCandidatePool.description: Candidates are filtered by playing time, role confidence, optional budget and the availability of statistical similarity evidence.

calculateSignals.title: Calculate decision signals
calculateSignals.description: The engine adds tactical role fit, spatial similarity, heatmap evidence, market advantage and age suitability.

applyEligibility.title: Apply scenario eligibility
applyEligibility.description: Each recruitment scenario applies its own minimum similarity, quality, reliability, role and age requirements.

scoreAndExplain.title: Score and explain
scoreAndExplain.description: Eligible candidates receive a scenario-specific score, rank, recommendation type and human-readable evidence.

evidence.title: How to read player evidence
evidence.description: Player values, percentiles and sample sizes answer different questions. They should be read together without treating missing evidence as measured performance.

output.label: Output
output.title: Raw and per-90 values
output.description: The reported output is the player's measured tournament value. Per-90 values normalize volume for playing time; they are not percentile scores.

positionContext.label: Position context
positionContext.title: Same-position percentile
positionContext.description: Percentiles compare the player with eligible peers in the same position group. A higher percentile means stronger expression of that metric.

peerSample.label: Peer sample
peerSample.title: What n represents
peerSample.description: The n value is the number of eligible same-position peers. Peer cohorts require at least 180 tournament minutes and 10 usable players.

evidenceState.label: Evidence state
evidenceState.title: Missing is not zero
evidenceState.description: Unavailable evidence remains missing. A measured zero is preserved as a real value and is never replaced with a neutral or invented result.

roleModel.title: From performance profile to tactical role
roleModel.description: The platform keeps statistical style, measured occupation and the final tactical interpretation distinct so each layer can be inspected independently.
roleModel.supportingDescription: Lateral profile, vertical profile and mobility profile describe how the player occupied and moved through the pitch. Role confidence expresses how strongly the available evidence supports the assigned role.

statisticalArchetype.title: Statistical archetype
statisticalArchetype.description: Describes how the player's tournament actions and performance metrics cluster statistically.

spatialRole.title: Spatial role
spatialRole.description: Describes where the player operated using average location, lane occupation, vertical zone and spatial spread.

finalRole.title: Final role
finalRole.description: Combines the statistical archetype with the measured spatial profile to produce the tactical role used by the recommendation engine.

statisticalSimilarity.title: Statistical similarity
statisticalSimilarity.description: A position-relevant comparison from the precomputed player similarity model. Candidates without a measured statistical similarity are excluded.
statisticalSimilarity.detail: This signal describes similarity, not whether the candidate is automatically the better player.

roleFit.title: Role fit
roleFit.description: Role fit awards 45 points for the same final role, 25 for the same archetype, 12 for the same spatial role, then 7, 6 and 5 points for matching lateral, vertical and mobility profiles.
roleFit.detail: The raw match score is moderated by the candidate's role-confidence level.

spatialSimilarity.title: Spatial similarity
spatialSimilarity.description: Average position, spatial spread, third occupation and lane occupation are standardized before calculating distance from the target profile.
spatialSimilarity.detail: When fewer than three usable spatial fields exist, the engine uses a neutral score of 50.

heatmapSimilarity.title: Heatmap similarity
heatmapSimilarity.description: Measured heatmap evidence includes cosine similarity, shared-zone occupation, lateral and vertical structure, peak zones and entropy.
heatmapSimilarity.detail: Missing heatmap evidence remains explicitly missing; only the decision score receives the configured neutral fallback.

marketAdvantage.title: Market advantage
marketAdvantage.description: The candidate's market value is evaluated relative to the target. Less expensive candidates generally receive a stronger financial-advantage signal.
marketAdvantage.detail: When the target has no usable market value, the candidate pool's market-value percentile is used instead.

ageSuitability.title: Age suitability
ageSuitability.description: Age suitability combines a general age curve with an adjustment based on the candidate's age difference from the target.
ageSuitability.detail: Its importance changes substantially by recruitment scenario.

playerQuality.title: Player quality
playerQuality.description: A tournament-derived quality signal helps prevent similarity alone from promoting candidates without sufficient performance level.
playerQuality.detail: Minimum quality requirements vary between immediate, development, value and short-term analysis.

dataReliability.title: Data reliability
dataReliability.description: Reliability represents how strongly the available tournament sample supports the player's calculated profile.
dataReliability.detail: Higher-risk scenarios can accept lower reliability, while immediate and short-term recommendations demand stronger evidence.

comparisonEvidence.title: Different views answer different questions
comparisonEvidence.note: Statistical similarity, spatial similarity and heatmap similarity are complementary signals. None of them replaces the others or proves that one player is superior.

measuredHeatmap.title: Measured heatmap
measuredHeatmap.description: The pitch shows observed tournament occupation. Heatmap density and average position are independent evidence sources displayed on the same coordinate system.

heatmapComparison.title: Heatmap comparison
heatmapComparison.description: Cosine similarity, occupation overlap, lateral and vertical structure, peak zones and entropy describe different aspects of spatial resemblance.

radarComparison.title: Radar comparison
radarComparison.description: Radar dimensions use position-relative percentiles. Same-position players can share one scale; cross-position players retain separate positional contexts.

scenarios.title: One candidate pool, four different decisions
scenarios.description: Every scenario filters candidates using its own eligibility rules and then applies a different weighting model. The weights below represent the current engine configuration.

immediate.title: Immediate impact
immediate.summary: Prioritizes tactical continuity, current quality and reliable evidence for first-team contribution now.

development.title: Development investment
development.summary: Accepts more tactical adaptation and places the strongest emphasis on age upside and future market potential.

value.title: Market value opportunity
value.summary: Balances tactical suitability with financial efficiency and places the largest weight on price advantage.

short_term.title: Short-term solution
short_term.summary: Targets experienced candidates and emphasizes role continuity, tournament quality and data reliability.

ranking.title: How score, rank and explanation are produced

paragraphs.weightedScore: The engine first calculates a weighted scenario score. A matching final role and statistical archetype can add scenario-specific bonuses. The result is then restricted to the 0–100 range.
paragraphs.tieBreaking: Candidates are ordered first by scenario score. Ties and close results are resolved using role fit, effective heatmap score, statistical similarity and player quality, in that order.
paragraphs.explanation: The explanation engine ranks available evidence and selects up to four distinct evidence groups. This prevents one type of evidence from dominating the complete explanation.

heatmapFallback.title: Neutral is not measured similarity
heatmapFallback.description: When direct heatmap evidence is unavailable, the measured heatmap fields remain missing. The configurable neutral score is used only inside the weighted decision model.

elite.label: Elite
elite.meaning: Exceptionally strong scenario fit across the weighted decision signals.

strong.label: Strong
strong.meaning: Convincing candidate with substantial evidence for the selected scenario.

good.label: Good
good.meaning: Useful recommendation with a credible, but less complete, overall case.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.meaning: Potentially relevant candidate requiring closer contextual scouting.

low.label: Low
low.meaning: Eligible for the scenario, but supported by comparatively weaker combined evidence.

limitations.title: What the analysis does not prove

paragraphs.sample: Tournament data represents a limited competitive sample. A strong tournament profile does not guarantee the same output across a full domestic season, another tactical system or a different physical environment.
paragraphs.marketContext: Market values are contextual estimates rather than transfer fees. Contract length, wages, registration rules, injury history, personality and club strategy are outside the current scoring model.
paragraphs.similarity: Similarity is not superiority. A candidate can resemble the target while being less productive, less reliable or unsuitable for the intended recruitment timescale.
paragraphs.decisionSupport: The platform is a decision-support system. Final recruitment decisions should combine this evidence with video, live scouting, medical review and broader club context.
